---
title: "Layouts"
subtitle: "Organising the page"
---

`fluidPage()` is a page based on a **grid 12 units wide**. On top of it, Shiny offers a few ready-made structures.

## See them

A sidebar, three tabs, and two columns inside the last tab. Click on the tabs:

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [viewer]
#| viewerHeight: 650
## file: ui.R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Layouts"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:",
                  choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars")),
      width = 3                       # the sidebar takes 3 of 12 units
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot")),
        tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary")),
        tabPanel("Two columns",
                 fluidRow(
                   column(6, h4("First column"), tableOutput("head")),
                   column(6, h4("Second column"), plotOutput("hist", height = "250px"))
                 ))
      ),
      width = 9
    )
  )
)
## file: server.R
library(shiny)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  dataInput <- reactive(get(input$dataset))

  output$plot    <- renderPlot(plot(dataInput()[, 1:2]))
  output$summary <- renderPrint(summary(dataInput()))
  output$head    <- renderTable(head(dataInput()))
  output$hist    <- renderPlot(hist(dataInput()[, 1], main = names(dataInput())[1]))
}
```

## How they are written

```r
fluidPage(                       # <1>

  fluidRow(                      # <2>
    column(6, ...),
    column(6, ...)
  ),

  sidebarLayout(                 # <3>
    sidebarPanel(...),
    mainPanel(...)
  ),

  tabsetPanel(                   # <4>
    tabPanel("Plot", ...),
    tabPanel("Summary", ...)
  )
)
```
1. The page: rows with columns, within a grid 12 units wide
2. A row with two columns, each 6 units wide (6 + 6 = 12)
3. Automatic layout with a sidebar (for the inputs) and a main area (for the outputs)
4. Tabs: only one is visible at a time

## The code

The code of the app above. You can edit it and press ▶.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [editor, viewer]
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 650
## file: ui.R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Layouts"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:",
                  choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars")),
      width = 3                       # the sidebar takes 3 of 12 units
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot")),
        tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary")),
        tabPanel("Two columns",
                 fluidRow(
                   column(6, h4("First column"), tableOutput("head")),
                   column(6, h4("Second column"), plotOutput("hist", height = "250px"))
                 ))
      ),
      width = 9
    )
  )
)
## file: server.R
library(shiny)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  dataInput <- reactive(get(input$dataset))

  output$plot    <- renderPlot(plot(dataInput()[, 1:2]))
  output$summary <- renderPrint(summary(dataInput()))
  output$head    <- renderTable(head(dataInput()))
  output$hist    <- renderPlot(hist(dataInput()[, 1], main = names(dataInput())[1]))
}
```

## Exercise

Move the dataset menu out of the sidebar and put it in a `fluidRow()` on top of the tabs. Change the widths of the two columns to 4 and 8.
:::
